clue.text: Hit man when given cheek at home

parts.note: as in 'as I left' means when I left

explanation.surface: A hired killer gets lip from someone while staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is a professional killer hired to murder a target, which is exactly what an assassin does.

clue.text: Cared passionately about a covered avenue of shops

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged word wraps the next piece
acting passionately means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone felt strongly about a shopping arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of Cared are rearranged as ARCDE and the A sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a roofed passage lined with retail units on either side.

clue.text: Gale erected cross — this may give the house extra protection

definitions.text: this may give the house extra protection

parts.note: a gale is a violent wind, a storm

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means stood upright, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, the cross in a church

explanation.surface: A storm puts up a cross, then the clue talks of protecting a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is the old word for the cross of Christ, often on a screen in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm door is an additional outer door fitted to shield the entrance from bad weather.

clue.text: Very little in street is attractive

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviation for the road

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Something tiny in the road turns out to be charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet describes something charming or pleasing, such as a sweet little cottage.

clue.text: ''Fancy meeting you here…'', as Gulliver might have said in Lilliput?

definitions.meaning: the surface reading: the stock remark on bumping into an acquaintance in an unexpected place

definitions.text: as Gulliver might have said in Lilliput?
definitions.meaning: the setter's reading: in Lilliput everyone and everything is tiny, so a visitor would remark on the size of the place

explanation.surface: A chance encounter prompts a familiar greeting, attributed to Swift's traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gulliver's Travels, Lilliput is the land of people six inches tall, so the stock phrase becomes literally true there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is what people say on meeting someone they know far from home, marvelling at coincidence.

clue.text: Close in feeding shark, say

indicators.note: feeding means being put into a mouth, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a shark is an example of a fish, as say signals

explanation.surface: A shark comes close while it is feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Close is the verb here, as in close a meeting, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To close something is to end or complete it, which is what finish means as a verb.

clue.text: Decoration that could make press angry

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: An award for some public figure might irritate the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Press suggests journalists, but it is the household chore of smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military medal for bravery, a decoration awarded to soldiers.

clue.text: I spot one inside with dope

indicators.note: inside says the numeral sits within the word for a small mark

explanation.surface: Someone notices a person carrying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope suggests drugs, but it is the slang word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is informal for a stupid person, a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Film, peak of achievement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1952 western starring Gary Cooper
second meaning: the climax or moment of greatest success

explanation.walkthrough: The western is famous for its showdown at midday, which gave the phrase its figurative sense of a decisive moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a classic Hollywood western, and the phrase also denotes the height or culmination of something.

clue.text: Women talk over a misconstrued hippie slogan

indicators.note: something misconstrued is taken the wrong way, so these words are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Women discuss a hippie catchphrase that has been misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the rallying cry of the 1960s counterculture opposing the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Conservative socks picked out

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A traditional pair of socks has been selected.
explanation.definitionFit: Chose is the past tense of choose, meaning selected from among alternatives.

clue.text: Could be salt making up shanty about Northern Ireland

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song wraps the abbreviation for the province

parts.note: a shanty is a sailors' song, a sea song
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An old sailor's song about Northern Ireland might be a bit salty.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt suggests a sailor, an old salt, but it is just a flavouring, one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is a typical example of a flavouring added to food to improve its taste.

clue.text: Cup of coffee — seem sad, upset, drinking it

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece is swallowed by the other
upset means knocked over and disordered, so those letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone looks miserable while sipping a small coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup used for serving strong black coffee, French for half-cup.

clue.text: Copper can join traffic dangerously

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer is allowed to drive into traffic recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman and can a verb, but they are the metal and a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to pull sharply into a gap in front of another vehicle, a risky manoeuvre.

clue.text: Loaded? Both row boat and row drunkenly

indicators.note: doing something drunkenly means doing it in a muddled way, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Two drunk people rowing a boat; loaded here hints at intoxication.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaded is slang for both drunk and rich; the clue's scene points to drunk but the answer means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for wealthy, and being worth a bob or two is a British idiom for having plenty of money.

clue.text: County type pair bamboozled, restricting runs

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the jumble holds the cricket abbreviation inside
bamboozled means confused, so the letters of those words are mixed up

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Two printers' typefaces are confused and slow down the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a county in the Republic of Ireland, famous from the wartime song.

clue.text: Adopted children disagreed

parts.note: to adopt something is to take it on
issue is the legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Adopted children had an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Adopted looks like it describes the children, but it is a separate verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with someone is to dispute or object to what they say.

clue.text: Pure drink makes a lot of money

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: A clean, wholesome drink turns out to be very profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is informal for winning or earning a large profit, as at a casino.

clue.text: Famous golfer shown entering cricket ground accompanied by North, British statesman

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the golfer goes inside the ground

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
Arnold Palmer, the American champion golfer
as in singing to the piano, meaning with it as accompaniment
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A star golfer appears at a cricket venue with someone named North, a British politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground, home of the MCC. Lord North is himself a British statesman, a decoy for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Palmerston was a Victorian Prime Minister and Foreign Secretary of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Skilful with it, a rod at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so these letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: A deft angler with a fishing rod out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means dexterous and clever in handling things or situations.

clue.text: Male leaving wringer in corner

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for a man goes away from the word

parts.note: a mangle is an old machine of rollers for wringing water from washing
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man walks away from an old laundry wringer in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is the point where two lines or walls meet, so a nook or corner.

clue.text: Understand Greek, like Prince

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
P is the abbreviation for Prince

explanation.surface: Following Greek is as hard as following a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend or take it in mentally.

clue.text: Fiend with moon out? Agreed

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A devil emerges under a full moon, and everyone concurs.
explanation.definitionFit: People of one mind share the same opinion, so they are in agreement.

clue.text: Scottish town producing the Spanish spirit

explanation.surface: A Scottish town makes Spanish liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests whisky from a Scottish distillery; here it is just gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray in north-east Scotland, near many whisky distilleries.

clue.text: A terrible flap on board barge in naval base

indicators.note: on board means aboard a vessel, so these pieces go inside the barge

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

indicators.note: terrible suggests a mess, so the next word's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: There is a dreadful panic aboard a barge in the naval harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A flap is a panic, but here only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow in Orkney was the Royal Navy's main anchorage in both World Wars.

clue.text: Gadget army medic used on US soldiers

explanation.surface: An army doctor tries out a device on American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, used on means placed after, so the medic follows the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, also spelt gizmo, is an informal word for a clever device or contraption.

clue.text: Cartoon character with soft drink, look

parts.note: to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure sips a fizzy drink and glances around.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the spinach-eating sailor of the comic strip and animated films.

clue.text: Part of church, part with Ten Commandments at the end, set out

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so the collected letters are arranged anew
at the end points to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A section of church with the Ten Commandments displayed at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten Commandments reads as a single phrase, but Ten is used whole and only the last letter of Commandments counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, running across the nave.
